transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

No, it is not safe to continue using your microwave in this condition.

You have correctly identified serious warning signs: sparking (arcing), blue flashes, and crackling noises. These indicate that electricity is jumping between metal surfaces or through air gaps inside the oven cavity. Continuing to use it can cause:

1.  Fire hazard – Sparks can ignite food residue, grease, or even damage internal components.
2.  Permanent damage – Arcing can destroy the magnetron (the component that generates microwaves), the waveguide cover, or the interior walls of the oven.
3.  Safety risk to you – In rare cases, severe arcing can lead to electrical faults or smoke emission.

### ✅ What You Should Do Now:

1.  Unplug the microwave immediately if it isn’t already unplugged.
2.  Do not use it again until it has been inspected and repaired by a qualified technician.
3.  Inspect the interior carefully (only when unplugged):
• Look for any metal objects left inside (e.g., foil, utensils, containers with metallic trim).
• Check if there is food residue or grease buildup on the walls, ceiling, or floor of the cavity. Burnt-on food can carbonize and become conductive, causing arcing.
• Inspect the waveguide cover (a small rectangular or square mica/cardboard-like panel on the right-hand side wall). If it’s charred, burnt, or damaged, this is a common cause of sparking and needs replacement.
4.  Clean the interior thoroughly if you find grease or food debris. Use a damp cloth with mild detergent, then dry completely. Never use abrasive cleaners.

### ❌ What NOT to Do:

• Do not attempt to repair internal components yourself unless you are qualified. Microwaves contain capacitors that can hold a lethal electrical charge even when unplugged.
• Do not ignore the issue or try to “test” it again after cleaning if sparks return.

### 🔧 Next Steps:

• If the waveguide cover is damaged, replace it (it’s an inexpensive part). You can find replacement parts for your Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ online using the full model number.
• If you’re unsure or if sparking persists after cleaning and removing all metal objects, contact Panasonic Customer Support or a certified appliance repair technician.

Your safety is paramount. When in doubt, err on the side of caution and get it professionally checked.
Thanks. I've unplugged it. I looked in and there's a cardboard-like panel on the right wall with a black burnt spot and greasy splatter on it. Is that the part you mean, and can I replace it myself?

Yes, that is exactly the part I was referring to. It’s called the waveguide cover (also known as the mica sheet or arcing shield). Its job is to protect the magnetron from food splatters while allowing microwaves to pass through. When it gets greasy or burnt, it can cause sparking and crackling noises.

### ✅ Can You Replace It Yourself?
Yes, you can replace it yourself if you’re comfortable with basic DIY tasks. Here’s how:

#### 1. Order the Correct Replacement Part
• Search for “Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ waveguide cover” or “mica sheet”.
• Ensure it matches your model exactly. You can find parts on Amazon, eBay, or from appliance repair suppliers like RepairClinic or PartSelect.

#### 2. Tools Needed
• A Phillips-head screwdriver (usually #2).
• A clean cloth.
• Mild detergent and water for cleaning.

#### 3. Steps to Replace the Waveguide Cover
   a. Unplug the microwave – Already done, but double-check.
   b. Remove the old cover:
• Locate the small rectangular or square panel on the right-hand wall of the oven cavity (usually near the top).
• It’s held in place by one or two screws. Remove them carefully.
• Gently pull off the burnt/damaged mica sheet.
   c. Clean the area:
• Wipe away any grease, carbon residue, or debris from the waveguide opening and surrounding area. Use a damp cloth with mild detergent, then dry thoroughly.
• Ensure no food particles are stuck near the magnetron vent (the hole behind where the cover sits).
   d. Install the new cover:
• Place the new mica sheet over the waveguide opening, aligning it properly.
• Secure it with the screws you removed earlier. Do not overtighten.
   e. Test cautiously:
• Plug in the microwave.
• Run a short test (e.g., heat a cup of water for 30 seconds) to ensure no sparking occurs.

### ⚠️ Important Notes:
• Use only mica-based waveguide covers – Do not substitute with metal, plastic, or other materials. Mica is heat-resistant and microwave-safe.
• If the burnt spot is extensive or if you notice damage to the surrounding wall or magnetron vent, consult a professional technician. Severe arcing can sometimes indicate deeper issues.
• Never operate the microwave without the waveguide cover – This will damage the magnetron quickly.

### 🛠️ If You’re Uncomfortable:
If you’d rather not DIY, take it to a qualified appliance repair service. The part itself is inexpensive (~$5–$15), but labor costs may apply.

Thanks. I'll cope with a clip-in part but I won't open the casing. Does the panel just clip in from inside the cavity, or do I have to take screws out and open the outside? Also, I noticed a wisp of smoke from that burnt spot once before it stopped when I turned it off. Is that a worry?

The waveguide cover on your Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is secured with screws, not clips. You do not need to open the outer casing or touch any internal components beyond the cavity wall. Here’s what you need to know:

### 🔧 How It’s Attached
• The mica sheet (waveguide cover) is held in place by 1–2 small Phillips-head screws on the inside of the oven cavity, typically near the top-right corner.
• You simply unscrew these, remove the old burnt sheet, clean the area, and screw in the new one. No external casing removal required.

### 🚨 Smoke Is a Serious Warning Sign
Yes, smoke is a concern. It indicates that:
• The mica sheet was overheating due to grease buildup or damage.
• Carbonized residue may have been igniting.
• Continued use could lead to fire risk or further damage to the waveguide or magnetron.

Since you stopped it promptly, you’ve likely avoided major harm. But do not use the microwave again until the mica sheet is replaced and the interior is thoroughly cleaned.

### ✅ Next Steps Recap
1. Order a replacement waveguide cover for your model.
2. Unscrew the old burnt sheet from inside the cavity.
3. Clean the area with a damp cloth (no abrasives).
4. Install
